name: Hearthstone Firearms Trail-357 'Pathfinder'
description:
The Hearthstone Trail-357 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum with a five-inch barrel and a stainless steel frame finished in a brushed satin that resists the elements. Hearthstone designed the Pathfinder for residents of the peripheral territories and rural settlements who need a reliable sidearm for outdoor carry in harsh conditions — dust, moisture, temperature extremes, and the unpredictable threats of the wastelands.

The Pathfinder is Hearthstone's best weapon by a wide margin. Where their Shelf-focused products prioritize minimum cost, the Trail-357 prioritizes ruggedness. The frame is overbuilt for the caliber, the cylinder lock-up is tight, and the internal parts are treated with a corrosion-resistant coating that keeps the action smooth even after weeks of exposure to gritty environments. The five-inch barrel extracts full velocity from .357 Magnum ammunition while keeping the weapon holsterable.

In the peripheral territories, the Pathfinder has become something of a standard. Settlement defense groups carry them, expedition teams pack them as backup, and the few individuals who still work the land between GLMZ's developed zones rely on them as multi-purpose tools — personal defense, pest control, and signal device. The weapon is also compatible with .38 Special for cheaper everyday carry.

tactical_use: A rugged outdoor revolver built for sustained reliability in harsh environments. The .357 Magnum chambering provides adequate stopping power for personal defense and wilderness threats. The stainless construction and corrosion-resistant internals maintain function in conditions that would compromise lesser weapons. Compatible with .38 Special for reduced-recoil applications.
cultural_context: The Pathfinder is the rare Hearthstone product that earns respect across the firearms spectrum. In the peripheral territories, it is the weapon that everyone recognizes and most people trust. Carrying a Pathfinder outside the city signals that you know what you're doing in the wastelands — or at least that you asked someone who does.
story_hooks: A Pathfinder is found in the wastelands with all six rounds fired and a dead owner — surrounded by seven dead things that nobody can identify. The sixth round is embedded in something that shouldn't exist.
Hearthstone begins marketing the Pathfinder to urban buyers as a 'heritage weapon,' prompting outrage from peripheral territory residents who consider it appropriation of their culture.

physical_description.visual_profile: A classic, purposeful revolver with a workmanlike presence. The Pathfinder presents as a dependable tool rather than a tactical showcase—a wide, robust cylinder dominating the silhouette, thick frame that suggests overbuilt durability, and a business-like five-inch barrel. The overall impression is frontier-ready: honest, utilitarian, built to last through seasons of hard use.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 26.5 cm | Barrel length: 12.7 cm | Frame width: 4.2 cm | Cylinder diameter: 4.8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but balanced—1.02 kg that settles naturally in the hand. Heavy enough to absorb recoil smoothly, light enough for extended carry without fatigue. The weight distribution favors control over quick-draw speed.
physical_description.primary_material: Stainless steel frame and cylinder. Internal components treated with corrosion-resistant polymer coating. Smooth trigger mechanism housing.
physical_description.finish: Brushed satin stainless steel across frame and cylinder—a flat, non-reflective surface that resists glare and corrosion equally. Micro-scratched texture from intentional manufacturing process, designed to hide field wear. No high-polish—every surface engineered for function over aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte silver-gray stainless with charcoal-black trigger guard and grip frame accents. Muzzle end shows faint bluish heat-treat marks where barrel meets frame.
physical_description.grip_texture: Walnut scales (traditional, weather-resistant hardwood) with subtle checkering for purchase even in wet conditions. Slightly rounded profile that sits comfortably in palm or holster. No aggressive angular edges—designed for hours of carry without chafing.
distinctive_features: Six-round cylinder with tight, audible lock-up clicks
Recessed ejector rod beneath barrel, flush-mounted
Visible internal coil springs visible through frame gaps (engineering honesty)
Wide, serrated rear sight adjustable for elevation
Front sight post with slight orange-amber tint for low-light targeting
Cylinder release lever positioned for right-handed operation
Hammer spur slightly oversized for gloved manipulation
Wear patterns: light streaking on frame sides from repeated holstering
Faint tooling marks on frame sides—evidence of careful machining
Small venting grooves along frame to reduce fouling accumulation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HEARTHSTONE FIREARMS stamp on left frame side in small serif letters. Trail-357 engraved along top of barrel in utilitarian script. Serial number on bottom of frame grip, stamped clearly. No tactical markings or posturing—purely informational.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field condition. Not pristine (that's not the design intent), but meticulously cared-for. Light scratches on the brushed finish are invisible against the satin. Cylinder shows slight carbon residue at the forcing cone from regular shooting. Grip wood may have subtle moisture marks from sweat and weather exposure, lending authenticity to the 'working tool' aesthetic.
